reasons.text: Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 30% of months
68% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Claimed tonnage in the busiest month would need 185% of the plant's connected load running non-stop (above 100% is physically impossible)
Category III share of certificates is 48%, +46% versus what its process route can produce
27% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.36x the cost floor)

inspection_checklist: Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Cross-check the certificate generation dates and category mix against the plant's process route and stock registers.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
